summary:
Developed by team Carbonauts for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our project is an interactive, AI-powered web platform designed to analyze and synthesize decades of NASA’s microgravity combustion research from the Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database.  

The platform addresses the critical challenge of spacecraft fire safety—especially in future lunar and Martian habitats where enriched oxygen environments dramatically increase flammability risks. By automatically classifying, summarizing, comparing, and interpreting complex studies, our tool extracts vital insights to help engineers design advanced prevention protocols, risk-tuned sensor detection systems, and suppression procedures.  

This is vital because fire in microgravity behaves unpredictably and poses a catastrophic threat to human space exploration. Ultimately, our solution bridges the gap between dense scientific data and actionable engineering, ensuring safer missions in space and inspiring technological safety improvements on Earth.
details:
Overview and Functionality

Carbonauts has developed an interactive, Superintelligence (SI)-powered web application designed to interpret, summarize, compare, and draw actionable conclusions from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Data Repository on microgravity combustion science. Functioning as an intuitive AI-driven data browser, the platform enables engineers and researchers to navigate complex experimental datasets through complementary pathways, combining a natural language conversational browser with a visual Data Library tab. Professors, graduate students, undergraduate students, aerospace researchers, and aerospace engineers can also use it.

Scientific Rigor and Architecture

To maintain scientific rigor, the AI engine operates under a near-zero hallucination architecture strictly grounded in verified NASA experimental files. Because of this safety-first design, if a specific detail cannot be confidently retrieved from the indexed documents, the system explicitly states that it does not know rather than fabricating an answer. This addresses severe information overload for aerospace engineers, distilling decades of dense technical documentation into structured insights across the three pillars of fire safety: prevention, detection, and extinction. By accelerating access to deep domain knowledge, the platform empowers teams to design safer spacecraft and mitigate fire emergencies rapidly.

Intended Impact

The ultimate intended impact of Carbonauts is to protect human lives and critical infrastructure as humanity expands into deep space, particularly in future lunar and Martian habitats or pressurized rovers where oxygen-enriched, reduced-pressure atmospheres significantly increase fire hazards. Beyond space exploration, transforming raw microgravity combustion data into actionable engineering insights also drives advancements in safety technologies on Earth.

Scalability and Future Roadmap

What we have designed for the hackathon functions as an initial demo, trained on a curated subset of documents due to technical constraints involving API limits and server space. However, our project architecture is highly scalable:

  • Direct PSI API Integration: Through the official PSI database API, the platform can seamlessly ingest and index all available studies directly, updating dynamically as new experimental records are added. Additionally, the system incorporates a dedicated studies list, ensuring that every AI-generated response provides precise, advanced citations referencing the exact studies utilized in each search.
  • Advanced Multidimensional Filtering: With expanded data capacity, the search engine can scale to support multidimensional parameter filters, environmental variables (such as oxygen concentration and pressure), and fuel types. Furthermore, the AI can be configured to output structured JSON data alongside fully rendered CSV datasets.
  • Interactive 3D Physics Simulator: With broader data integration, the platform could evolve to incorporate a real graphical simulator built with PyTorch—featuring a 3D virtual environment that models flame behavior under specific environmental conditions and microgravity. This would serve as a powerful tool for testing and prediction prior to conducting physical laboratory experiments.

About the project

Tools and Technologies

From a technical and creative standpoint, the current application was built using Python and Streamlit, deployed via Streamlit Community Cloud, and powered by the Google AI Studio API alongside a Hugging Face token, with development managed in Visual Studio Code and GitHub.

Creativity and Team Considerations

Rather than presenting NASA’s repository as a static archive, our team reimagined scientific exploration by pairing natural language search with a structured visual library, supported by a cohesive brand identity designed in Adobe Illustrator, interactive UI/UX motion prototypes built in Adobe After Effects, and audiovisual production edited in DaVinci Resolve. Throughout the process, our multidisciplinary team structured its workflow using the Design Thinking Canvas and Google Workspace, balancing near-zero hallucination reliability, intuitive user experience under pressure, and rigorous aerospace validation.

Team Lineup

Irune – Project Leader & Aerospace Safety Specialist

Background: Industrial Technology Engineering student.

Role: Directs general team coordination, and schedule planning. Additionally, she leads the technical validation of experimental data on microgravity combustion and flammability.

Haritz – Team Management, Art Direction & Quality Control

Background: Industrial Technology Engineering (Master's student).

Role: Supervises project cohesion and internal organization, provides criteria in art direction, and conducts comprehensive product reviews to ensure every technical and visual detail meets the highest standards.

Alejandro – Data Engineer, AI & UX/UI Designer

Background: Industrial Technology Engineering (Master's student).

Role: Responsible for processing dataset files from NASA's PSI repository and developing the Superintelligence (SI) model. He also designs the visual and interactive architecture of the web platform to translate complex metrics into clear, actionable visualizations.

Ugaitz – Art Director, Graphic Design & Audiovisual Production

Background: Graphic Design student.

Role: Gives visual identity to the project. In charge of global graphic design, brand aesthetics, and the editing and assembly of the official video used to present our solution to the jury.
